```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(targets)
library(hexbin)
library(ggrepel)
library(stringr)
library(viridis)
library(patchwork)
library(igraph)
library(sf)
library(gridExtra)
library(grid)

devtools::load_all(quiet = TRUE)
```

If we want to build an AEP for algae, we need to start by working out what our relevant datasets are. Off the cuff, the most important are:
- Marine (fjord and ocean) concentrations
- Maybe marine sediment concentrations?
- Algae concentrations

I don't actually know if free-living algae have all that much to do with copper, and I presume that macroalgae (which is all we have data for) doesn't directly uptake copper from sediment, because they don't have roots. So if we were to sketch out the required matrices:

1. Algae tissues (first degree)
2. Algae habitat - marine water (second degree)
3. Matrices adjacent to marine water - marine and freshwater sediment, freshwater, atmosphere
4. Emissions/sources


Start in the middle and work out.

# Algae

```{r}
algae <- tar_read(load_literature_pqt) |> filter(SPECIES_GROUP == "Algae")

algae |>
  group_by(SAMPLE_SPECIES, REFERENCE_ID) |>
  reframe(n = n()) |>
  arrange(n)
```

We have a lot of data for algae, but it's macroalgae rather than microalgae. We probably can't assume consistent internal concentrations across such a biodiverse set of taxa, but nevertheless it's a starting point. I can (and will) go looking for more papers, but I want to work with what I have first.

## Fucus vesiculosus
a.k.a Bladderwrack

Via Worms is found in [Arctic](https://www.marinespecies.org/aphia.php?p=taxdetails&id=145548#distributions) regions, but is it an arctic species? 

## Ascophyllum nodosum
a.k.a Knotted wrack


Generally cosmopolitan distribution across the Atlantic. Cold tolerance uncertain, but probably sufficient for our purposes.

# Distribution of Copper Concentrations

There's one improbably high outlier in the dataset. We'll remove anything over 50mg/kg dry weight. Black Angel (2017) results are reported with SDs, while Vannmiljø data is just points. But, we need to be careful about sites, dates, and especially campaigns.

The below plot code uses the thresholds for coastal marine waters, since we don't have a background level for algae. We infer that seaweed bioaccumulate copper!

```{r}
#| label: algae-comparison
threshold_data <- generate_copper_thresholds() |>
  filter(ENVIRON_COMPARTMENT_SUB == "Marine/Salt Water")


algae_pointrange <- algae |>
  filter(MEASURED_VALUE <= 50) |>
  mutate(
    SITE_COMMENT = SITE_COMMENT |>
      stringr::str_remove("^.*?\\."),
    SITE_NAME = SITE_NAME |> stringr::str_remove("Vannmiljø Station")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = SITE_NAME, x = MEASURED_VALUE, colour = MEASURED_VALUE)) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c() +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = UNCERTAINTY_LOWER, xmax = UNCERTAINTY_UPPER)) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_color() +
  geom_vline(
    # TODO: Fix cvolours, add labels to lines.
    data = threshold_data,
    aes(xintercept = THRESHOLD_VALUE, color = TITLE_SHORT),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.8,
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = str_wrap(SITE_COMMENT), x = UNCERTAINTY_UPPER + 0.5),
    colour = "black",
    hjust = 0
  ) +
  labs(y = "Site Code", x = "Measured Value (mg/kg)") +
  facet_wrap(
    facets = vars(MEASURED_UNIT_STANDARD),
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Otherwise, our standard workup should be something like:
- Any temporal patterns?
- Any spatial patterns?
- Any site selection rationale or nearby sources we might expect to drive elevated concentrations?

```{r}
#| label: algae-hexmaps
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(viridis)
library(patchwork)

world_map <- map_data("world")
# reduce bbox size
get_study_area_bbox <- function() {
  st_bbox(c(xmin = -65, xmax = 40, ymin = 55, ymax = 75))
}

algae_hex <- algae |>
  filter(!is.na(LONGITUDE), !is.na(LATITUDE))

sample_size_map <- algae_hex |>
  ggplot(aes(x = LONGITUDE, y = LATITUDE)) +
  geom_polygon(
    data = world_map,
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
    fill = "grey95",
    colour = "grey80",
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  stat_bin_hex(
    bins = 100,
    colour = NA
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "magma",
    trans = "sqrt",
    name = "Sample count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Sample Size",
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.title = element_blank()) +
  coord_fixed(
    ratio = 2,
    xlim = c(
      get_study_area_bbox()[[1]],
      get_study_area_bbox()[[3]]
    ),
    ylim = c(
      get_study_area_bbox()[[2]],
      get_study_area_bbox()[[4]]
    )
  )

mean_conc_map <- algae_hex |>
  ggplot(aes(x = LONGITUDE, y = LATITUDE, z = MEASURED_VALUE)) +
  geom_polygon(
    data = world_map,
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
    fill = "grey95",
    colour = "grey80",
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  stat_summary_hex(
    fun = function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    bins = 100,
    colour = NA
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "viridis",
    name = "Mean concentration\n(mg/kg dry & wet)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.title = element_blank()) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean algae concentration by hexbin",
  ) +
  coord_fixed(
    ratio = 2,
    xlim = c(
      get_study_area_bbox()[[1]],
      get_study_area_bbox()[[3]]
    ),
    ylim = c(
      get_study_area_bbox()[[2]],
      get_study_area_bbox()[[4]]
    )
  )
```

Sample sizes are highest in the Oslofjord area, and concentrations are unusually high in mid-Norway (Tisler & Orkedalsfjorden). Why?

Finally, any time trends? We're unlikely to see much massively illuminating, because we don't have a great deal of data for any given site.

```{r}
#| label: algae-time-trends
algae_timetrend <- algae |>
  filter(MEASURED_VALUE <= 50) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = SAMPLING_DATE, y = MEASURED_VALUE, group = SITE_NAME)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_minimal() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, aes(colour = SITE_NAME)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

algae_timetrend


algae_pointrange + (sample_size_map / mean_conc_map / algae_timetrend)
```

Well, that's helpful.

Can we be a bit more spatially intelligent without having to do lots more work?

```{r}
# let's cluster our points based on proximity.
distance_matrix <- st_as_sf(algae, coords = c("LONGITUDE", "LATITUDE")) |>
  st_set_crs(4326) |> # tell sf these are WGS84 lat/lon
  st_distance()

# for the sake of argument, sites within 20km of each other
# from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77179007/group-spatial-points-by-distance-in-r-how-to-group-cluster-spatial-points-so-gr
binary_matrix <- matrix(
  as.numeric(
    distance_matrix
  ) <
    20000,
  nrow = nrow(distance_matrix)
)


g <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(binary_matrix)

# grouped algae sites
algae_grouped <- algae
algae_grouped$site_group <- factor(components(g)$membership)


# create sf (keep original lon/lat columns)
algae_sf <- st_as_sf(
  algae_grouped,
  coords = c("LONGITUDE", "LATITUDE"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE
)

centroids <- algae_sf |>
  st_transform(3857) |> # metric projection for accurate centroids
  group_by(site_group) |>
  summarize(geometry = st_combine(geometry), .groups = "drop", n = n()) |> # combine points per group
  st_centroid() |> # centroid of multipoint
  st_transform(4326) # back to lon/lat (if needed)

# centroids is an sf point layer with site_group and geometry
centroids_xy <- centroids |>
  mutate(
    LONGITUDE = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
    LATITUDE = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]
  )

groups_map <- ggplot(
  data = centroids_xy,
  aes(x = LONGITUDE, y = LATITUDE)
) +
  geom_polygon(
    data = world_map,
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
    fill = "grey95",
    colour = "grey80",
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_label_repel(
    aes(colour = site_group, label = site_group),
    max.overlaps = 100
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +

  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title = element_blank()) +
  coord_fixed(
    ratio = 2,
    xlim = c(
      get_study_area_bbox()[[1]],
      get_study_area_bbox()[[3]]
    ),
    ylim = c(
      get_study_area_bbox()[[2]],
      get_study_area_bbox()[[4]]
    )
  )

# strings to remove from comments:
remove_patterns <- c(
  # urls / emails / unicode quotes
  "(?i)https?://\\S+|www\\.\\S+|\\S+@\\S+",
  # parenthetical / bracket content
  "\\s*\\([^)]*\\)|\\s*\\[[^]]*\\]",
  # report codes like 01.01-385, 2021/09, 2290-12 etc.
  "\\b\\d{1,4}(?:[\\.\\-/]\\d{1,4})+\\b",
  # simple station / sample codes L1, L2, Stasjon 3, Station 4
  "\\bL\\d+\\b|\\bStasjon\\s*\\d+\\b|\\bStation\\s*\\d+\\b",
  # short code fragments like '01', '02' as standalone tokens (avoid years by requiring non-4-digit)
  "\\b(?!\\d{4}\\b)\\d{1,3}\\b",
  # report words (Norwegian / English) and common report prefixes
  "(?i)rapport(?:\\s+nr\\.?|nr\\.?|nummer|:)?.*?\\b|(?i)report(?:\\s+no\\.?|\\s+nr\\.?|\\s+nr)?",
  "(?i)rapporter?\\b|(?i)reference(?:\\s+site)?\\b|\\bref\\.?\\b",
  # vannmiljø / vm markers and resipient/resipientundersøkelse noise
  "(?i)vannmilj[oø]\\b|\\bvm\\b|(?i)resipient(?:unders[kq]økelse|unde)?",
  # 'Vm Emission Source' and variants; Miljøgifter etc.
  "(?i)vm\\s*emission\\s*source|(?i)miljøgifter\\b|(?i)miljøgifter\\s+i",
  # contractor / org names (common Norwegian consultancies + generic ' AS' suffix)
  "(?i)akvaplan-?niva|niva\\b|nina\\b|ramb[ao]ll\\b|norconsult\\b|asplan\\s+viak\\b|ngi\\b|ng\\&i\\b|APN|AS",
  "\\b\\p{Lu}[\\p{L}'’\\-]+(?:\\s+\\p{Lu}[\\p{L}'’\\-]+)*\\s+AS\\b",
  # page / folio / table refs
  "\\bpg?\\.?\\s*\\d+\\b|\\bp\\.\\s*\\d+\\b",
  # measurement / unit fragments that clutter comments
  "\\bmg/kg\\b|\\bmg/kg\\s*dry\\b|\\bmg/kg\\s*wet\\b|\\bSD\\b|\\bStandard\\s+Deviat(?:ion|ions)\\b",
  # stray punctuation sequences and repeated separators
  "[,;:\\|]{2,}|--+|\\.\\.+",
  # original comment
  "Original Comment:",
  "Emission Source:",
  "rsøkelse",
  "Vannmiljø Station",
  "Station"
)

# Some keywords for source characterisation:
# deponi
# industri*

# Example: combine and apply
combined <- str_c(remove_patterns, collapse = "|")
# then use: df |> mutate(SITE_COMMENT = str_remove_all(SITE_COMMENT, regex(combined, ignore_case=TRUE)) |> str_squish())

algae_sites_groups <- algae_grouped |>
  mutate(
    SITE_COMMENT = str_remove_all(
      SITE_COMMENT,
      regex(combined, ignore_case = TRUE)
    ) |>
      str_squish(),
    SITE_NAME = str_remove_all(
      SITE_NAME,
      regex(combined, ignore_case = TRUE)
    ) |>
      str_squish()
  ) |>
  reframe(
    .by = "site_group",
    condensed_name = paste(unique(SITE_NAME), collapse = ";"),
    condensed_comments = paste(unique(SITE_COMMENT), collapse = ";"),
    condensed_site_types = paste(
      unique(SITE_GEOGRAPHIC_FEATURE),
      collapse = ";"
    ),
    condensed_site_subtypes = paste(
      unique(SITE_GEOGRAPHIC_FEATURE_SUB),
      collapse = ";"
    ),
    n_sites = n(),
    n_samples = sum(MEASURED_N)
  )


# wrap long text in character columns
df_wrap <- algae_sites_groups |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ str_wrap(.x, width = 100)))

groups_table <- tableGrob(df_wrap, rows = NULL)

grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(groups_table)

groups_map / groups_table
```

# EPEQ Assessment

We have a fairly disordered dataset here, but rather than wait for the perfect one we will attempt to do the assessment (badly) so we can continue to build the network.

```{r}
#| label: epeq_assessment
# So, our relevant data:

# just based on wet weights right now
algae_wet_weight <- algae |> filter(MEASURED_UNIT_STANDARD == "mg/kg (wet)")

# mean +- SD
algae_mean <- algae_wet_weight |>
  reframe(mean_value = mean(MEASURED_VALUE_STANDARD, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull()
algae_sd <- algae_wet_weight |>
  reframe(sd_value = sd(MEASURED_VALUE_STANDARD, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull()
# sample size
algae_n = algae_wet_weight |> reframe(n = n()) |> pull()
# lines of evidence
# counting Vm as one feels wrong, but what can you do?
algae_lines_of_evidence <- algae_wet_weight |>
  reframe(.by = REFERENCE_ID) |>
  nrow()
# Essentiality (1-3)
algae_essentiality_score = 3
algae_essentiality_justification = "Copper is an essential component in photosynthesis (source?). Thus algae must have a system for the controlled uptake of copper."
# Plausibility (1-3)
algae_plausibility_score = 3
algae_plausibility_justification = "As above, the role of copper in photosynthetic organisms (including algae) is well studied and understood."
# Evidence (1-3)
algae_evidence_score = 3
algae_evidence_justification = "Although the studied dataset contains limited evidence on copper concentrations in algae, measured concentrations are well in excess of background water concentrations. Strong specific evidence is not considered necessarily in light of the overall scientific consensus."
# Quantification (1-3)
algae_quantification_score = 2
algae_quantification_justification = "Copper kinetics and metabolism in algae are assumed to be well understood, although such literature was not included in the study criteria."

# Plus justifications

# so our evidence is shaped like (for nodes)
# build long EPEQ table for algae
epeq_algae_long <- tibble::tibble(
  parameter = c(
    "matrix",
    "mean",
    "sd",
    "n",
    "n_lines_of_evidence",
    "essentiality_score",
    "plausibility_score",
    "evidence_score",
    "quantification_score"
  ),
  value = c(
    "Biota (Aquatic) - Seaweed - Shoot Tips",
    as.character(algae_mean),
    as.character(algae_sd),
    as.character(algae_n),
    as.character(algae_lines_of_evidence),
    as.character(algae_essentiality_score),
    as.character(algae_plausibility_score),
    as.character(algae_evidence_score),
    as.character(algae_quantification_score)
  ),
  justification = c(
    NA_character_,
    NA_character_,
    NA_character_,
    NA_character_,
    NA_character_,
    algae_essentiality_justification,
    algae_plausibility_justification,
    algae_evidence_justification,
    algae_quantification_justification
  )
) |>
  tibble::as_tibble()

epeq_algae_long
```

# Marine Water

Obviously there's going to be loads of this. Some important questions:
1. Is there actually any significant difference between fjords, estuaries, near and far ocean?
(_some_ fjords are likely to be quite contaminated, but will that show up in our data?)

In fact, our data is (currently) all fjords, because Vannmiljø doesn't monitor open ocean (as far as I know... but what about O&G monitoring?) 

```{r}
marine <- tar_read(load_literature_pqt) |>
  filter(ENVIRON_COMPARTMENT_SUB == "Marine/Salt Water")

marine |>
  group_by(
    SITE_GEOGRAPHIC_FEATURE,
    SITE_GEOGRAPHIC_FEATURE_SUB,
    REFERENCE_ID
  ) |>
  reframe(n = n()) |>
  arrange(n)
```

Marine water gets the same analysis as algae, although it's likely to be more complicated due to the greater amount of data. We won't show the full comments here, we simply don't have the space.

```{r}
# wrap long text in character columns
df_wrap <- marine_sites_groups |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ str_wrap(.x, width = 100)))

groups_table <- tableGrob(df_wrap, rows = NULL)

grid::grid.newpage()
grid::grid.draw(groups_table)

groups_map / groups_table
```

# Gap-Filling

Initial research suggests it's difficult to say how much copper is "in algae". We can still do AEP stuff, but the evidence is necessarily going to be weak. Some key points:

- Copper is also a stressor and essential nutrient in microalgae, but knowledge is spotty
https://www.mdpi.com/2305-6304/10/9/527

I guess we can start with the information we have and hopefull extend it if/when we get some more data...
